observations.code_quote: - `signals-scout-unused-features/` — feature-usage audit: the clickable elements and pages people can reach and still barely use. Its discriminator is reach vs use: distinct clickers of an element over distinct viewers of the page it lives on, after templated `data-attr` families (`row-<record name>`) collapse to one item, so a tiny share on a well-visited page is signal and a low count on a quiet page is not. Gives each candidate the first matching cause from a fixed ladder (dead code, not trackable, behind a flag, too new, hard to find, rare by design, faded, else reachable and not used) and files one report per area. The inventory comes from the project's own telemetry, which cannot see a never-clicked element; a pinned `repositories` checkout adds the code inventory (never-used items, dead code, first-shipped dates, owners). Audits at most weekly behind a scratchpad date and reports deltas after the first audit. Bundles `references/queries.md`. Flag debt is the feature-flags scout's territory, flow conversion is product-analytics', and launch effect is pr-follow-up's.
